headline: A 2017 federal law that sets rules and goals for science, technology, and research agencies such as the National Science Foundation and NIST.
what_it_does: The law directs the National Science Foundation to keep its grant review criteria and to issue guidance that stresses transparency and accountability. It renames and changes several federal research programs, including EPSCoR, and asks NIST to study cybersecurity standards, including quantum-resistant cryptography. It also sets up working groups and advisory panels on reducing research paperwork, STEM diversity, and STEM education, and it directs agencies to fund various STEM education and outreach grants.

who_it_affects.group: Researchers who receive federal science grants
who_it_affects.how: The Office of Management and Budget must create a working group to look for ways to reduce administrative burdens while keeping federally funded work transparent and accountable.

who_it_affects.group: Institutions that apply for National Science Foundation grants
who_it_affects.how: The NSF must keep its intellectual merit and broader impacts review criteria and issue updated guidance on the merit review process.

who_it_affects.group: Students and K-12 schools in STEM subjects
who_it_affects.how: The NSF must award grants for research on engaging students in kindergarten through 8th grade in STEM and for computer science education.

who_it_affects.group: Women and underrepresented groups in STEM fields
who_it_affects.how: The NSF must award grants aimed at increasing their participation, and a Center of Excellence must be set up to collect and share related information.

who_it_affects.group: Undergraduate students at colleges and universities
who_it_affects.how: Each federal agency must recommend to the President ways to expand research opportunities for undergraduates.

who_it_affects.group: Manufacturers working with NIST's Hollings Manufacturing Extension Partnership
who_it_affects.how: The law revises the requirements for this partnership program, which helps smaller manufacturers adopt new technology.
The NSF must fund Innovation Corps training and mentoring on commercializing research.

when_it_takes_effect: The law was enacted on January 6, 2017, and many provisions set their own deadlines for agencies to act, which the summary does not list.
